Right then, Nepal Under-19 have a way too steep mountain to climb as they have 297 on the board to chase. They are out of contention to reach the semis, but they will look to finish on a high. Can they pull up a shocker? Or will India Under-19 carry on to maintain their dominance in the World Cup? We shall find out soon. Chase is coming up shortly...

As for the Nepal Under-19, their pacers, Gulshan Jha and Aakash Chand, started off well to put India on the back foot. The ball did get some purchase earlier, but as the game progressed, it got easier to bat. Uday Saharan and Sachin Dhas then kept on batting and stitched a 215-run partnership. Gulshan Jha picked up three wickets for his side and was the pick of the bowlers, while Aakash Chand has one in his bank. Overall, it was not a good outing for the Nepal bowlers.

The Mangaung Oval, Bloemfontein, just witnessed one of the greatest partnerships of the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup! To start with, India Under-19 were rocked early and were reeling at 62/3 inside 14 overs of play. The skipper, Uday Saharan, and Sachin Dhas then joined hands and carried on with the flurry of runs. Sachin Dhas was the aggressor who took the bowlers to the cleaners, while the skipper played as a second fiddle. Both then stitched a partnership of 215 runs as Sachin Dhas fell to 116 on a shorter delivery. The skipper fell in the last over after scoring a hundred.

A single to end the over and Gulshan Jha has bowled an absolute gem of an over to restrict India Under-19 to under 300 runs. Digs it short and hits the deck hard outside off, Musheer Khan tries to pull but gets beaten by the extra bounce. The batters pinch a quick single and is called byes.

Gear up for an exhilarating clash between the formidable India U-19 side and the determined Nepal U-19. The India Under-19 team has been exceptional in the tournament, winning four games with scores of over 250 in their last two outings. The Super Sixes stage of the ICC Under 19 Cricket World Cup 2024 is firmly underway and in Match number 7, we have a group 1 clash where reigning champions and high-flying India Under-19 will go up against neighbours Nepal Under-19 at the Mangaung Oval in Bloemfontein. A clash that can be seen as David vs Goliath as the Indian side has been near perfect so far in this competition and have blown away teams, raking up 200-plus run margin victories for fun and they will be looking to seal a semi-final berth by doing more of the same to their neighbours. Nepal Under-19 on the other hand fought hard in their final group game against Afghanistan and made it to the Super Sixes stage but they have already lost a game in this stage of the competition against Bangladesh. Nepal Under-19 will be looking to simply do their best and hope that the Indian side makes a few mistakes that they can pounce on and maybe pull off a miraculous victory. As far as India Under-19 is concerned, they made a mockery of their opponents in the group stage and even in their first Super Sixes game against New Zealand, they put on a magnificent show and at the heart of it all was Musheer Khan, the brother of Sarfaraz Khan, who was recently called up for India's Test series against England and the younger brother struck a second ton in a row to set up the game for his side. The bowling then came good Saumy Pandey picked up four wickets and Musheer Khan even got a couple of wickets himself as well, as the Indians routed the Kiwis by bundling them out for just 81 runs. They have plenty of other exciting cricketers in their ranks as well and you never know who might step up on a given day which makes them the team to beat in this competition. Nepal Under-19 have played some good cricket in patches but haven't been able to perform together as a team. Their skipper, Dev Khanal has been prolific and has scored runs in every game with the likes of Gulshan Jha and Subash Bhandari doing more than a decent job with the ball in hand and Bhandari has even shown his prowess with the bat as well. Their main weakness is the inconsistency of the top order which will be in focus yet again as they face a pretty stern test from the Indian bowling attack. A win for Nepal Under-19 will see them pull off the heist of the tournament whereas a win for India Under-19 will only solidify their status as the 'favourite' in this competition. Who are you backing for the win?
